newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 97 deficit could be up to 3.8 pct/GDP - paper.
newsitem.headline: French 97 deficit could be up to 3.8 pct/GDP - paper.

text.p: France's new Socialist government has been told the budget deficit could be 3.7 percent or 3.8 percent of gross domestic product this year and 4.5 percent of GDP in 1998, the newspaper Les Echos reported on Wednesday, citing figures from the finance ministry's budget division.
It said the estimates from the traditionally pessimistic division "should be taken with caution" and included the risks of overruns.
The estimates would put the public deficit way above the strict three percent criterion set in the Maastricht treaty for countries wishing to take part in a single currency.

The ministry's separate forecasting division had slightly more optimistic expectations, estimating this year's deficit would be less than 3.5 percent of GDP and below four percent next year, the newspaper said.

"The risk of state budget overruns would be between 10 and 20 billion francs and less than 10 billion for the social security budget, relative to an earlier anticipated deficit of 30 billion francs," the forecasting division said.

In April, the newspaper Le Monde said a worst-case scenario produced by ministry experts pointed to a public deficit of up to 3.8 percent this year. But the conservative government, which was defeated in the May 25/June 1 parliamentary election, rejected the report, saying the trend up to then showed it was on course to meet the Maastricht criterion.
The new Socialist government is planning an audit of state finances which will give a clearer picture of whether public deficits can be limited this year to three percent of GDP.
